evidence.quoted_text:
def claim_run_dir(self):
        base = Path(self.args.record_dir)
        resolved = base.resolve()
        root = self.root.resolve()
        require(resolved != root and root not in resolved.parents,
                "--record-dir must be outside the deployment checkout")
        base.mkdir(mode=0o700, parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        require(not base.stat().st_mode & 0o077,
                "private record directory must have mode 0700: " + str(base))
        name = ("run-" + time.strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ", time.gmtime())
                + "-" + uuid.uuid4().hex[:6])
        self.run_dir = base / name
        self.run_dir.mkdir(mode=0o700)
        return self.run_dir
evidence.reason: The claim_run_dir path creates the record base and then creates the run directory, but never fsyncs the record base or its parent after those mkdir calls. durable_write(path, receipt) at line 598 syncs the receipt and run directory, not the newly created run-directory entry in the record base. If the process claims the host admission and then the machine loses power, POSIX permits the run directory entry to vanish even though the admission hold persists, losing the recovery receipt with prior_sha and trigger state. The fix is to fsync the record base after self.run_dir.mkdir(), also fsync the parent when base was newly created, and fail admission if either sync fails. This is an ordinary crash-consistency repair, not a new protective requirement.
